## Q1 2026 Sales Snapshot for the E-commerce Team
A small dashboard should focus on **trend, efficiency, and spend-to-return**. The dataset shows steady growth overall, with April as the strongest month across orders, revenue, and ad spend.

## Recommended Dashboard Charts
### 1) Monthly Trend Line Chart
Use a line chart with 3 series: **Online Orders**, **Revenue**, and **Ad Spend** across Jan–Apr 2026.
- Best for showing month-to-month momentum
- Highlights the dip in March and rebound in April
- Good executive view for overall business direction

### 2) Revenue vs Ad Spend Combo Chart
Use clustered bars for **Revenue** and **Ad Spend**, with a line for **Revenue per Ad Dollar** or **ROAS proxy**.
- Best for marketing efficiency review
- Shows whether higher spend is translating into proportionally higher revenue
- Useful for budget planning

### 3) Orders and Revenue Efficiency Bar Chart
Use grouped bars for **Orders** and **Revenue per Order** by month.
- Best for checking basket value quality, not just volume
- Helps explain whether growth came from more orders or higher order value
- Good for operations and merchandising teams

## Key Metrics and What to Watch
| Metric | Jan | Feb | Mar | Apr | What it shows |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Online orders | 420 | 510 | 470 | 560 | Demand volume trend |
| Revenue | 18,600 | 21,400 | 20,100 | 24,300 | Sales growth trend |
| Ad spend | 2,900 | 3,200 | 3,000 | 3,500 | Marketing investment |
| Revenue per order | 44.29 | 41.96 | 42.77 | 43.39 | Average order value proxy |
| Revenue / ad spend | 6.41x | 6.69x | 6.70x | 6.94x | Spend efficiency proxy |

## Main Insights to Highlight
- **April was the best month**: highest orders, revenue, and ad spend.
- **Revenue grew faster than orders overall**, which suggests the team is improving monetization, not just traffic.
- **March was a soft spot** for orders and revenue, but the drop was modest and recovered strongly in April.
- **Ad efficiency improved over time**: revenue per ad dollar rose from **6.41x** in January to **6.94x** in April.
- **Average order value stayed fairly stable** in the low-to-mid 40s, so the main growth driver was volume, not a large basket-size jump.

## Executive Summary
The business showed a healthy upward trend across Q1 2026, ending with a strong April performance. Orders increased from 420 to 560 and revenue rose from 18,600 to 24,300, while ad spend also increased but at a slower pace than revenue, indicating improving marketing efficiency. For a small e-commerce team, the most useful dashboard should combine a monthly trend view, a revenue-vs-spend efficiency chart, and an orders-to-value chart so leadership can quickly see growth, efficiency, and where to optimize spend.

- Dashboard design basics: https://www.tableau.com/learn/articles/data-visualization-tips
